key_insight: An automated machine-learning and Bayesian optimization workflow can optimize gas lift rates directly from historical production data, without downhole gauges or multi-rate tests.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, scalable control method for unconventional oilfields where facility limits and missing downhole measurements make conventional optimization difficult.
method: Train an ML model to forecast the gas lift performance curve from historical time-series production data.
Use Bayesian optimization to search for the gas injection rate that maximizes production under facility capacity constraints.
Deploy the workflow across wells to automate recommendation of optimal gas lift settings.
evidence_signal: In the Bakken pilot on 30 wells across 5 pads, the workflow achieved more than 5% average production uplift and was later deployed across 200+ gas lift and PAGL wells.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and representativeness of historical production data, and the model may need retraining when operating conditions or facility constraints change.
paper_title: A Machine-Learning-Based Gas Lift Optimization Workflow for Unconventional Fields
